messages.text: What is non-signaling tester, and which product-related measurement decisions depend on understanding it?

A non-signaling tester is an RF measurement tester used when the DUT is not tested through a live/signaling connection; in the Rohde & Schwarz Wi‑Fi production context, all WLAN device production RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time, and the R&S CMP180 is positioned as the tester optimized for that purpose [34]. By contrast, the R&S CMX500 is positioned as a one-box signaling tester; the RAW evidence only confirms CMX500 as a “5G one-box signaling tester” [37].
| Product-related measurement decision | What depends on understanding “non-signaling” | Supported context |
|---|---|---|
| Choose CMP180 vs. CMX500 | Use R&S CMP180 for production-phase non-signaling RF measurements; use R&S CMX500 for signaling-oriented R&D / one-box signaling workflows [34][14][37]. | CMP180 is described as a production-phase non-signaling RF measurement tester [14], while CMX500 is described as a signaling tester in the Wi‑Fi 7 R&D context [14] and as a 5G one-box signaling tester in RAW evidence [37]. |
| Decide which CMP180 measurement options are needed | CMP180 option selection depends on whether the measurement is non-cellular, cellular, WLAN, MIMO, PER, Bluetooth, UWB, LTE, NR FR1, etc. [8]. | The CMP180 option list includes non-cellular measurements pack 1, cellular measurements pack 1, WLAN IEEE 802.11be SISO measurements, WLAN true MIMO 2x2/4x4, WLAN true MIMO 5x5/6x6, WLAN packet error rate acknowledgement measurements, LTE measurements, and NR FR1 measurements [8]. |
| Decide bandwidth and frequency coverage for production RF tests | CMP180 supports cellular and non-cellular technologies including Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz, with bandwidths up to 500 MHz [34]. | This determines whether the tester configuration can cover the intended Wi‑Fi / cellular production measurements [34]. |
| Decide MIMO production test scaling | A single CMP180 integrates two analyzers, two generators, and two sets of eight RF ports for 2x2 MIMO testing; two CMP180 instruments can be combined for four analyzers and generators for 4x4 MIMO access points [34]. | Understanding the non-signaling production role determines whether one box is enough or whether two CMP180 units are needed for 4x4 MIMO access-point testing [34]. |
| Decide whether a 480 MHz WLAN waveform test is production-relevant or only exploratory | CMP180 is shown validating a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode, but the source frames it only as a potential waveform candidate for the yet-to-be-defined Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn, not as a formal Wi‑Fi 8 specification [34]. | This affects whether to treat 480 MHz WLAN loopback as a supported demonstration capability rather than a finalized conformance requirement [34]. |
| Avoid confusing signaling OTA / R&D tests with production non-signaling RF measurements | CMX500 supports WLAN signaling and WLAN TX measurements, while CMP180 is the production non-signaling RF measurement tester in the Wi‑Fi 7 production context [4][34]. | CMX500’s role includes signaling and application-style test capabilities [4], whereas CMP180 is tied to time-saving production RF measurements in non-signaling mode [34]. |

CMX500 Callbox
[[CMX500 Callbox]] 是 [[CMX500_Callbox]] 簡報中對 [[R&S CMX500]] 的 use-case 定位：用一台 callbox 快速建立 DUT 連線，進行 RF、mobility、application、NTN、WLAN / cellular desense、pre-conformance 與 non-signaling R&D 驗證。

R&S CMX500 › 產品定位
依 [[CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100]]，[[R&S CMX500]] 是 universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution，支援最新 3GPP [[5G NR]] technology，適用於 device testing，涵蓋 [[LTE]]、[[NR FR1]]、[[NR FR2]]，並支援 non-standalone（NSA）、standalone（SA）、FDD 與 TDD。

依 [[CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32]]，[[R&S CMX500]] 也提供：

- [[NR FR1]] / [[NR FR2]] signaling 與 TX measurements。
- [[LTE]] signaling、LTE-DTC / direct-to-cell communication、LTE measurements。
- [[NB-IoT]] / NB-NTN signaling。
- [[WLAN]] signaling 與 WLAN TX measurements，涵蓋 802.11a/b/g/n/ac、802.11ax、802.11be、802.11bn 與 2x2 MIMO。
- [[Fading]]、[[AWGN]]、[[BLER]]、[[CSI report]]、[[Throughput measurement]]、[[PER measurement]]。
- Application test、IP traffic analysis、IMS / audio / [[POLQA]]。
- GUI、graphical scripting、Python-based [[XLAPI]] 與 [[SCPI]] remote control。

A non-signaling tester is an RF measurement tester used when the DUT is not tested through a live/signaling connection; in the Rohde & Schwarz Wi‑Fi production context, all WLAN device production RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time, and the R&S CMP180 is positioned as the tester optimized for that purpose [34]. By contrast, the R&S CMX500 is positioned as a one-box signaling tester; the RAW evidence only confirms CMX500 as a “5G one-box signaling tester” [37].
| Product-related measurement decision | What depends on understanding “non-signaling” | Supported context |
|---|---|---|
| Choose CMP180 vs. CMX500 | Use R&S CMP180 for production-phase non-signaling RF measurements; use R&S CMX500 for signaling-oriented R&D / one-box signaling workflows [34][14][37]. | CMP180 is described as a production-phase non-signaling RF measurement tester [14], while CMX500 is described as a signaling tester in the Wi‑Fi 7 R&D context [14] and as a 5G one-box signaling tester in RAW evidence [37]. |
| Decide which CMP180 measurement options are needed | CMP180 option selection depends on whether the measurement is non-cellular, cellular, WLAN, MIMO, PER, Bluetooth, UWB, LTE, NR FR1, etc. [8]. | The CMP180 option list includes non-cellular measurements pack 1, cellular measurements pack 1, WLAN IEEE 802.11be SISO measurements, WLAN true MIMO 2x2/4x4, WLAN true MIMO 5x5/6x6, WLAN packet error rate acknowledgement measurements, LTE measurements, and NR FR1 measurements [8]. |
| Decide bandwidth and frequency coverage for production RF tests | CMP180 supports cellular and non-cellular technologies including Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz, with bandwidths up to 500 MHz [34]. | This determines whether the tester configuration can cover the intended Wi‑Fi / cellular production measurements [34]. |
| Decide MIMO production test scaling | A single CMP180 integrates two analyzers, two generators, and two sets of eight RF ports for 2x2 MIMO testing; two CMP180 instruments can be combined for four analyzers and generators for 4x4 MIMO access points [34]. | Understanding the non-signaling production role determines whether one box is enough or whether two CMP180 units are needed for 4x4 MIMO access-point testing [34]. |
| Decide whether a 480 MHz WLAN waveform test is production-relevant or only exploratory | CMP180 is shown validating a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode, but the source frames it only as a potential waveform candidate for the yet-to-be-defined Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn, not as a formal Wi‑Fi 8 specification [34]. | This affects whether to treat 480 MHz WLAN loopback as a supported demonstration capability rather than a finalized conformance requirement [34]. |
| Avoid confusing signaling OTA / R&D tests with production non-signaling RF measurements | CMX500 supports WLAN signaling and WLAN TX measurements, while CMP180 is the production non-signaling RF measurement tester in the Wi‑Fi 7 production context [4][34]. | CMX500’s role includes signaling and application-style test capabilities [4], whereas CMP180 is tied to time-saving production RF measurements in non-signaling mode [34]. |
